_meta.source: gszep, "Speed limits, not walls" (2026), Who holds leverage, from mines to models
_meta.shares: Percent of each stage, by country group. Values and notes are copied unchanged from the published model.
_meta.weights: Stage weight at physical share s, linearly interpolated between w[0] (s=0), w[1] (s=0.5) and w[2] (s=1). Copied from the published model.
_meta.confidence: Our reading of the source note: "rough average"/"least certain" -> low, otherwise medium.
_meta.replicate_years: Team estimate, not from the source. Range of years a determined rival would need to build a substitute. Low confidence.

stages.name: Mining
stages.note: My average of where ore is mined, 2025 (USGS), over rare earths, copper, cobalt, nickel and tungsten; gallium is not mined on its own. Congo mines 74% of cobalt, Indonesia 67% of nickel, Chile, the Congo and Peru together 49% of copper, and China 69% of rare earths and 79% of tungsten. Chinese firms own many of the mines in the Congo and Indonesia.
stages.replicate_note: New mines take a decade or more from discovery to output.

stages.name: Mineral refining
stages.note: My rough average of where minerals are refined (tungsten: mined), 2025, over magnet rare earths, copper, gallium, tungsten, cobalt and nickel. China refines about 90% of magnet rare earths, 47% of copper, 76% of cobalt and makes 99% of gallium; Indonesia refines 45% of nickel, much of it in Chinese-owned plants.
stages.replicate_note: Refineries can be built in a few years, but skills and permits are slow outside China.

stages.name: Magnets & robot parts
stages.note: My rough average of strong magnets (94% made in China), precision robot gears (mostly Japanese firms) and industrial robots (by maker nationality).
stages.replicate_note: Magnet plants are quicker to build than precision gear know-how is to copy.

stages.name: Power & data-centre hosting
stages.note: Where data centres use electricity, 2024. Newly built AI capacity leans further towards the US.
stages.replicate_note: Data-centre shells go up in 1–2 years; grid connection is the bottleneck.

stages.name: Grid equipment
stages.note: My rough blend of transformers (where made; China about 60% by one industry estimate) and gas turbines (maker nationality). The least certain row.
stages.replicate_note: Transformers and gas turbines have multi-year order backlogs.

stages.name: Chip materials
stages.note: My rough average of silicon wafers (Japanese firms 44%), light-sensitive chemicals (about 60–75%), glass cloth (about 85–90%) and insulating film (over 95%) in chip packages, and high-purity quartz (mostly mined in North Carolina).
stages.replicate_note: Specialist chemicals and films depend on process know-how held by a few firms.

stages.name: Lithography & chipmaking tools
stages.note: Chipmaking equipment sales by maker nationality, 2025, my estimate from analyst rankings. One Dutch company makes every machine for the finest printing step (EUV).
stages.replicate_note: EUV took about two decades; no rival machine is close.

stages.name: Leading-edge chips & packaging
stages.note: Where the most advanced chips are made and packaged, late 2025; my estimate from company capacity shares. Most is in Taiwan.
stages.replicate_note: New leading-edge fabs abroad take 3–5 years to reach volume.

stages.name: AI memory (HBM)
stages.note: Revenue by maker nationality, Q2 2026: two Korean firms and one American. US rules have limited sales to China since December 2024.
stages.replicate_note: Memory makers outside Korea are ramping, but yields lag.

stages.name: AI chip design
stages.note: Share of AI computing power shipped, by designer nationality, late 2025.
stages.replicate_note: Chip design talent moves fast; software ecosystems move slower.

stages.name: Installed AI computing power
stages.note: Where AI supercomputers are, in a large sample from early 2025. Five US companies own over 70% of the world's AI computing power.
stages.replicate_note: Installed compute follows money and power within a few years.

stages.name: Notable AI models
stages.note: Notable AI models released in 2025, by developer nationality. In one ranking from March 2026, the top four developers were all American.
